title: A fair measure for uncertain impressions

captions.energy: Distinguishing imagination from what is known
captions.emotions: Feeling satisfied by a proportionate assessment

meaning: Your shared view can preserve a fair measure when you distinguish an impression from what is actually known.
text: A shared view sometimes becomes clearer through precisely named uncertainty. Justice in the physical position of Ajna suggests comparing impressions with known details. The Moon in energy supports wanting to distinguish imagination from what is established. Justice in emotions feels satisfaction in a fair, proportionate assessment. Its first role concerns how you examine something; its second concerns feeling that a conclusion describes no more than its grounds allow. Both of you may feel comfortable with knowledge that is limited but understandable.

Suppose you listen to a short recording of a courtyard in the evening. Rustling sounds suggest rain although the recording leaves this uncertain. **A fair assessment preserves an impression while naming its boundary.** Comparing audible sounds reveals which details produced the image. You can now describe a resemblance to rain while leaving its source open. This formulation feels satisfying: a personal response is heard without presenting it as an established event. Imagination remains part of the experience under its own name.

Difficulty arises if enjoying precision turns every impression into a reason for examination. Conversation then leaves little space for images even when nobody is making a factual claim. Wanting to distinguish layers preserves proportion: an image can remain an image and still have every right to appear in your discussion.
